title: Layered dataset transformers and deterministic prompt mutation service for stable profile generation
creator: Marisa Chen
description: Problem: Profile generation for onboarding models is brittle when datasets or prompt variants are generated nondeterministically. Small sampling or prompt-perturbation differences produce metric variance that complicates model pinning and rollout decisions. Scope: build a lightweight, deterministic prompt mutation service plus a layered dataset transformer pipeline that produces reproducible variant manifests and stratified slices. Integrate outputs into the benchmark harness so generated performance profiles (latency, tokens-per-output, quality deltas) are stable across runs and include strong provenance metadata for version pinning. Success looks like identical profile metrics across repeated runs with same seed, deterministic manifest files stored next to profile artifacts, and an updated publisher that attaches dataset+variant fingerprints to the profile catalog entry.
acceptance_criteria: Running the harness with --seed=<hash> against same model+dataset yields identical metrics (token counts, mean quality, latency p50/p95) across 3 repeat runs
Profile publisher writes a catalog entry that includes: model_version_pin, dataset_manifest_sha256, variant_manifest_id, harness_commit and a human-readable changelog
Profiling run can produce both deterministic and stochastic variant sets via a single flag (--deterministic=true|false)
Integration tests in CI validate fallback behavior: if a pinned-variant isn't available on a target infra, runtime falls back to compatible variant family and publisher records the fallback event
Documentation (Console + internal Confluence) describing how to interpret variant fingerprints and how they map to rollout/fallback policies
tasks: Design layered transformer API: canonicalizers, token-aware truncator, normalization, paraphrase perturbation (seeded)
Implement deterministic prompt mutation service (HTTP + local lib) with seeded PRNG and replayable mutation logs
Add variant manifest schema and storage path in artifact bucket; include per-variant deterministic hash and provenance fields
Wire harness runner to accept variant_manifest_id and produce per-variant metrics and failure traces
Extend profile publisher to attach dataset and variant fingerprints to catalog entries and emit rollback metadata
Add CI integration tests that run a small synthetic workload in deterministic mode and assert metric stability
End-to-end perf runs for 3 internal models and publish sample profiles to the staging catalog
Document API and add examples to onboarding playbook and console UX notes for profile pinning
comments: 2025-02-03 - Triage: Identified variance in onboarding profiles caused by prompt paraphrasing step. Assigned to Diego. (Marisa)
2025-02-05 - Design sync: Agreed on layered approach (canonicalize -> normalize -> seeded-paraphrase). PM requested that variant manifests include human-friendly labels. (Diego, Priya)

2025-02-09 - Decision: Use deterministic PRNG with explicit seed passed through harness rather than relying on system randomness. Trade-off: slightly less coverage for stochastic paraphrases but strong reproducibility guarantees. (Design review notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deterministic+Prompt+Mutations)

2025-02-11 - Implementation update: Core transformer lib implemented with pluggable steps. Added token-aware truncation to reduce bias from tokenization differences across runtimes. Unit tests added. (Diego)

2025-02-14 - PM feedback: Include variant severity (minor/major) to help rollout UI show expected delta. Also asked for a fallback recording field when publishers detect missing variant at deployment. (Priya)
2025-02-16 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/harness/pull/681. Running integration perf runs in staging. (Diego)

2025-02-18 - QA: CI deterministic test flaked once due to timeouts on staging infra; increased timeouts and retriggered. Observed identical quality metrics across two repeated runs after fix. (QA: Anika)
notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) Full stochastic mutation coverage vs strict determinism — we chose deterministic-by-default with an opt-in stochastic mode; (2) Store all variant text vs store diffs — storing manifests (+ compressed diffs) keeps artifact sizes small while retaining replayability. Longer-term: consider a shared variant registry that multiple teams can reference to avoid duplication.
